title: Uploaded files have no backup anywhere: a restore brings back the storage rows but not the avatars, post images and Loom originals they describe

source.ref: section 7, Not restored; OWN-082 rehearsal 2026-09-29; ADR-1625

detail:
FILED 2026-09-29 by OWN-082 (ADR-1625). MEASURED, NOT INFERRED: the Supabase Backups page says "Database backups do not include objects stored via the Storage API", and the restore dialog lists storage objects and storage settings among what a restore does not carry. The rehearsal copy restored all 526 storage.objects rows (equal to live) and none of the files they describe. So every uploaded file (avatars, post images, Loom originals and renditions, library-media) exists in one place only, and a deleted bucket, a bad delete loop or a lost project loses it for good. Searched the backlog before filing: no row covers a file backup.

THE ASK, a ruling because every option costs money or a new account: (a) a scheduled copy of the storage buckets to a second provider (an S3-compatible bucket such as Cloudflare R2 or AWS S3, driven by a GitHub Actions job over Supabase Storage's S3-compatible endpoint), which needs a new account, a credential in the repo secrets and a monthly storage bill; (b) a copy to a second bucket inside the same Supabase project, cheap but it dies with the project and so only covers a bad delete; (c) accept the risk for now, like PITR in ADR-1625, with a revisit trigger. Whichever is picked, the rehearsal cadence in RUNBOOKS section 7 then also rehearses a file restore.

Not agent work until ruled. A ruling of (a) or (b) turns into a build row with a probe; (c) closes this row with the revisit trigger written into an ADR.

verify.evidence: 2026-09-29: OPEN. docs/RUNBOOKS.md section 7 states no backup of storage files exists (Backups page wording; rehearsal copy had 526 storage.objects rows and no files). Closes on the owner's ruling: a file backup that has run once, or the risk accepted in an ADR with a revisit trigger.
